issues.description: Captures any issues that occurred while deserializing from filesystem

defaultFiles.description:
If a request is made for a resource directory, we check if that directory contains any of the these files and
generate a 302 Found response to the complete path. This is also known as an "index page" or "default document".

By default, the file "index.html" is checked, but if this configuration specifies other files, those will be
checked first.

@see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_server_directory_index

rootPath.description:
If the root path is accessed, and none of the #defaultFiles are valid there, this path is used. This allows
a {@link Ann.Restful @restful endpoint} to be used for example.

If used, the server will return a 302 [Found](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status/302)
response so that the browser will have the correct path.

cacheControl.description:
If desired, file responses can be returned with a custom `Cache-Control` header with this value. For example,
"max-age=86400" would allow the resource to be cached for a day and "no-cache" would force the browser to
revalidate the cache each time.

In fact, "no-cache" is the default since {@link UiService} supports `ETag` / `If-None-Match`.

Note that if the path matches #fingerprintRegex, #fingerprintedCacheControl is used _instead_.

@see https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Cache-Control
@see https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/If-None-Match

fingerprintRegex.description:
Regular expression to match a fingerprint suffix. This is used to trigger a different `Cache-Control` directive
specified in #fingerprintedCacheControl. The file must still exist with this exact path; this only serves to
change which header value is returned.
